A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same susceptibility-based interpretability research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original susceptibility measurements, trajectory PCA, comparisons with ablation and loss, and token-level analyses on a small transformer.

after.justification: v3 reports original empirical results, including per-token PCA, additional training seeds, sampling-variability analyses and comparisons with direct logit effects.

M1.justification: v3 extends structural inference with separate per-layer PCA of per-token susceptibility matrices and associates their components with token patterns. v1 used dataset/checkpoint susceptibility matrices for PCA, which remain in v3 Appendix G. The covariance estimator, local SGLD sampling and mixture-probe procedure are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions study next-token model structure using Pile subsets and the separate GitHub-code corpus. The new pattern and seed analyses use retained data. Philpapers remains in metric comparisons despite losing its dedicated catalogue subsection. The Pythia additions concern model scale and computational cost, without documenting a new corpus or task.

E2.justification: The comparisons with zero-ablation loss differences and original token losses are retained. v3 Appendix H adds an evaluated comparator: token-averaged direct logit effects calculated from the unembedding and head-output matrices, motivated by Gurnee et al. and Lad et al.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a substantial evaluation protocol for per-token PCA: 20,000 sampled tokens per dataset, separate analyses by layer, and pattern frequencies among the top positive and negative 1% and 10%. It also adds token aggregation for the direct-logit comparison and scaling measurements on Pythia-410M and Pythia-1.4B. The earlier checkpoint schedule, mixture ratio and core SGLD settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds circuit-recovery checks across training seeds, sensitivity to token sampling, all-token versus induction-token susceptibility distributions, and a test of the hypothesized connection to direct logit effects. It removes some earlier analyses, including the context-position variance plot, top-1,000 token-frequency analysis and Enron token-loss table. The original trajectory PCA is retained as supporting evidence.

E5.justification: v3 reports three additional independently trained models, giving four training seeds, and introduces means and standard deviations across ten independent draws of 20,000 tokens per dataset for PCA pattern percentages and head loadings (Appendices I–J). Both versions report four SGLD chains; the new variability estimates do not represent an increase in that chain count.

E6.justification: v3 adds per-token PCA, pattern-enrichment, cross-seed and direct-logit results and revises many retained measurements. The aggregate/per-token agreement diagnostic changes from r=0.817 and slope=15.992 to r=0.958 and slope=9.794. GitHub-all head 0:0's total susceptibility changes from 17,816 to 26,219 (v1 Table 1; v3 Table 2). The original trajectory-PCA variance percentages are retained in Appendix G.

T1.justification: v3 states the main covariance identity exactly for an h-independent observable, replacing v1's treatment of h-dependent observables with an O(1/n) term. It adds the population per-token integration identity and proof in Lemma A.1. Appendices D.4–D.5 replace the diagonal, mode-aligned expansion with a general mode-pair expansion, while v1's absolute-bigram derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The central claim of a linear-response interpretability framework that separates functional structures in a 3M-parameter transformer remains. v3 adds a more specific headline contribution: attributing recovered circuits to data patterns and explaining their balance of expression and suppression. v1 framed the demonstrated structural inference primarily as preliminary validation.

C2.justification: v3 develops an explicit expression/suppression interpretation and associates per-token PCs with word segmentation, the induction circuit and, more tentatively, bracket matching. It links context-length effects to induction-pattern suppression and reports no simple correspondence with direct logit effects. New limitations address SGLD hyperparameter sensitivity, correlated samples, component-wise sampling costs and the uncertain adequacy of PCA for larger models.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the 5,000-token tokenizer, BOS handling, detailed pattern-selection rules and additional data-mixing instructions. It replaces the TPU/runtime descriptions with A100 allocations and runtimes and adds scaling-cost formulas and Pythia cost measurements in Appendix C. These are substantial documentation changes; the underlying SGLD hyperparameters and dataset-access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around suppression, self-repair, ensemble behavior and prediction/suppression neurons, adding discussion of work such as McGrath et al., McDougall et al., Gurnee et al. and Rushing and Nanda. It also adds Bayesian influence-function references, including Giordano and Broderick and Iba. This extends v1's narrower ablation and influence-function discussion.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, contribution statements and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. Much of v1's theory and main empirical discussion moves into reorganized appendices, while per-token structural inference becomes the main results narrative. v3 also adds an appendix guide and dedicated limitations, reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v3 adds pattern-enrichment heatmaps, per-token PCA loading plots, distribution comparisons, direct-logit plots and seed/variability displays. Existing token visualizations are redrawn with per-head z-score coloring, and many figures are relocated. Several earlier displays disappear, including trajectory projections, the trajectory scree plot and the context-position variance plot; these changes go well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 left the data-pattern interpretation of its trajectory PCs substantially uncertain. v3 makes that interpretation more concrete through quantified pattern enrichment, circuit correspondence across four training seeds and sampling-variability checks (Section 4.2; Appendices I–J). These substantially strengthen the evidence for structural inference, alongside clearer organization and explicit limitations. Local reporting regressions remain: v3 Table 3 retains sums inconsistent with its revised positive and negative totals. Those errors do not outweigh the broader evidential gains.
